message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Build & Test

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "develop" ]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6

    - name: Set up JDK
      uses: actions/setup-java@v5
      with:
        java-version: '21'
        distribution: 'temurin'
        cache: gradle

    - name: Grant execute permission for gradlew
      run: chmod +x gradlew

    - name: Build libraries
      run: ./gradlew :vbpd-core:assembleRelease :vbpd:assembleRelease :vbpd-reflection:assembleRelease

    - name: Run tests
      run: ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest

    - name: Run code quality checks
      run: ./gradlew detekt ktlintCheck

    - name: Generate coverage report
      run: ./gradlew koverXmlReport

    - name: Upload test results
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
      with:
        name: test-results
        path: |
          **/build/test-results/
          **/build/reports/tests/

    - name: Upload coverage reports
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
      with:
        name: coverage-reports
        path: |
          **/build/reports/kover/

    - name: Upload build artifacts
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
      with:
        name: vbpd-libs-builds
        path: |
          vbpd-core/build/outputs/aar/*.aar
          vbpd/build/outputs/aar/*.aar
          vbpd-reflection/build/outputs/aar/*.aar",
  "rationale": "The workflow is a Gradle/Android build-and-test triggered on push to develop. It already caches Gradle via setup-java cache: gradle, so adding a separate actions/cache for ~/.gradle/caches (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) is contraindicated because an equivalent cache already exists. There is no matrix, so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST does not apply, and there are no scheduled runs or measured duration history for the schedule/timeout patterns. The applicable reviewed optimization is P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: runs on the same branch represent the same workflow and a newer push supersedes an older check; this is build/test rather than release/deployment, and scoping the concurrency group by workflow+ref keeps branches isolated. Adding concurrency with cancel-in-progress cancels superseded in-progress runs while the latest run still completes fully, preserving every build/test/coverage/upload step and required-check coverage. No permissions, secrets, publishing/deployment, or new network access are introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]
}
